newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC, India's Crompton plan telecom venture in India.
newsitem.headline: NEC, India's Crompton plan telecom venture in India.

text.p: NEC Corp said on Monday it has agreed with Indian electrical engineering firm Crompton Greaves Ltd (CGL) to set up a joint venture in India this autumn to make telecommunications equipment.
The joint venture, NEC CG Telecom Systems Pvt Ltd, will be capitalised at about 500 million yen and will be 51 percent owned by NEC and the rest by Crompton, an NEC spokesman said.
The firm's headquarters will be located in Bangalore in southern India.
The telecom devices that the joint venture is expected to produce will include very-small aperture terminals and synchronous digital hierarchy microwave systems, it said.
Very-small aparture terminals are land-based telecom relay stations that can beam microwave messages to communications satellites.
The new firm is expected to start manufacturing next spring. It will aim for sales of five billion yen in the first year and 20 billion yen in 2000, the spokesman said.
Crompton Greaves is a group firm of Thaper financial group in India.
